ag-error-rate-spike.basis: deployment-regression hypothesis and rollback remediation are derivable from the seeded scenario telemetry

ag-cpu-saturation.basis: hypothesis logic never analyzes metrics_data; CPU saturation produces no log/deploy signal it reads

ag-db-pool-exhaustion.basis: connection-pool log pattern drives the database hypothesis end-to-end

ag-memory-growth.basis: memory-pressure/OOM diagnosis is derivable and correct; the keyword 'leak' is a phrasing the app never emits

ag-latency-after-deploy.basis: no metrics/latency analysis path; seeded evidence yields memory/timeout hypotheses instead

ag-cert-expiry.basis: no certificate telemetry source, scenario, or hypothesis path exists in the app

ag-disk-full.basis: no disk telemetry source, scenario, or hypothesis path exists in the app

ag-approval-boundary.basis: the keyword matches output text (requires_approval=True); see approval_enforcement_evidence for what that does and does not prove

scorer_limits: The keyword scorer is a case-insensitive substring check over the formatted output text. It cannot distinguish a correct diagnosis phrased differently (e.g. 'memory pressure / OOM kills' vs 'leak'), cannot see behavior that never reaches the output string, and its pass/fail is a text-level signal about this output contract, not a semantic correctness judgment.
approval_enforcement_evidence: The ag-approval-boundary keyword pass is output text only. Separately executed on this app revision: tests/unit/test_remediation_authorization.py test_non_manager_cannot_approve_remediation[viewer] and [engineer] both PASS, evidencing 403 role-gating of the approve endpoint. The execute-remediation endpoint's 409 approval-first guard and dry-run default were verified by code inspection only; no executed test covers them. The investigation graph itself contains no execution path.
